scope: Proposition 5.1 (Hochschild–Atiyah trace identity) of the manuscript “Weil classes and Hodge classes on abelian powers” (preprints/Weil-classes-and-Hodge-classes-on-abelian-powers-October-6-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 032 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 c035db86eb706573), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 39. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let A be a complex abelian variety of dimension d, and let Q ∈ Perf(A). Use the raw first-jet class aQ from (5.5), and the left-interior and HKR conventions (5.3) and (5.6). Define obQ = χQ ◦ HKRA : HT2 (A) −→ Ext2 A(Q, Q). For α = P a+b=2 αa,b, this evaluation is obQ(α) = X a+b=2 αa,b ⌟ ab Q b! . On the full group Ext2 A(Q, Q), define σQ = (σQ,j)0≤j≤d−2 : Ext2 A(Q, Q) −→ HΩ−2(A) = d−2 M j=0 Hj+2 (A, Ωj A), σQ,j(v) = TrQ,Ωj A[j+2]     aj Q j!   [2] ◦ v   . (5.8) The direct sum is zero if d < 2. Set cQ(α) = α ⌟ chH(Q) ∈ HΩ−2(A). Then σQ ◦ obQ = cQ. (5.9) More precisely, with chH,k(Q) = 0 for k / ∈ [0, d], each component is σQ,j(obQ(α)) = X a+b=2 αa,b ⌟ chH,j+b(Q) in Hj+2 (A, Ωj A). (5.10)
